purpose: This combination is used as a mouthwash to help kill germs in your mouth, reduce plaque buildup on your teeth, and help prevent gingivitis, which is redness and swelling of the gums. It also helps freshen your breath. Using it regularly as part of your daily oral hygiene routine can help keep your mouth healthier.
how_it_works: These four ingredients work together as natural antiseptics, meaning they kill or stop the growth of the bacteria and germs that live in your mouth. Each ingredient attacks the outer covering of bacteria, breaking it down and destroying the germs before they can cause harm to your teeth and gums. Think of it like a team of cleaners working together to wipe out the bad bugs in your mouth.
common_side_effects: Some people experience a temporary burning or stinging sensation in the mouth, especially when first starting to use it. You may also notice a slight temporary numbness or tingling on your tongue or gums. Some people find the taste strong or intense at first, but this usually becomes more tolerable over time.
warnings: Do not swallow this mouthwash — spit it out completely after rinsing. Keep it out of reach of children under 6 years old, as swallowing it can be harmful to young children. If you have mouth sores or very sensitive gums, check with your dentist before using. Avoid using it right after brushing with fluoride toothpaste without rinsing your mouth with water first, as it may reduce the fluoride benefit. If irritation or allergic reactions develop, stop using it and speak with your doctor or pharmacist.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older, rinse your mouth with about 20 mL (roughly 4 teaspoons or the fill line on the bottle cap) for 30 seconds, then spit it out. Use it twice a day — once in the morning and once at night — after brushing your teeth. Do not eat or drink for 30 minutes after use for best results.
